name: How does a spillway compare to a traditional pool waterfall?

mainEntity.name: How does a spillway compare to a traditional pool waterfall?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both spillways and waterfalls add dynamic water features, they differ in design and water flow. A spillway typically involves water flowing smoothly from a defined edge, often a raised spa or basin, into the main pool, creating a uniform sheet or stream. Waterfalls, conversely, are designed to emulate natural cascades, often incorporating rocks or other landscaping elements for a more organic, uneven flow. Spillways tend to be more contemporary and integrated, while waterfalls offer a more rustic or naturalistic appearance. Your choice depends on the desired aesthetic and sound for your outdoor space.
acceptedAnswer.description: Spillways offer a smooth, defined water flow from a raised edge, while waterfalls mimic natural cascades with an organic, uneven flow, differing in aesthetic and sound.
